answer.rationale: Latency on the write path began climbing roughly 30 minutes after a release went out 2 hours ago, making the release the most proximate and reversible cause. Rolling back is the fastest way to restore write-path latency without losing customer writes, and it does not preclude failover or capacity work in the next window if the rollback does not resolve it. Regional failover is higher-risk during settlement peak (write-heavy traffic raises the chance of write loss or divergence mid-shift), and circuit breakers/read-replica routing don't fit a write-path symptom. Memory b1 supports rollback as a low-impact recovery lever, and b6 (staged gating) implies the release pipeline supports safe reversal. I am verifying b1 because the whole decision hinges on rollback being genuinely safe and effective here. Confidence is moderate because the release-latency correlation is not yet confirmed causation.
